phase: 29 — HCM detector popup-ownership investigation v2 (diagnosis only)
harness: chapter/qa-hcm-detector-p29.html — full-pass diagnostic: same node list, same order, same synchronous click-then-read and same running prevHead as qa-engine.js run(). Production files untouched.
headline: NO RELIABLE POPUP OWNERSHIP SIGNAL WAS FOUND IN THE EXISTING ARCHITECTURE. In addition, the full pass OVERTURNS the Phase-27 false-positive verdict.

step1_inventory.reason: qa-engine.js:286 emits HEADWORD_COLOUR_MISMATCH with detail {span, head} only. The baseline stores no headword text, so surface/headword identity cannot be read from it for any record — it is only observable at runtime.
step1_inventory.runtimeObservation: across 4,237 nodes in six full passes, only 2 rendered popups had a headword differing from the clicked surface (both in b2-15, case-only differences). Case-insensitively, ZERO genuine lemma/inflection cases were observed. The loose fallback headText !== prevHead therefore protects a case that may not exist in this corpus.

sourceRead: chapter-app.js:1385 — let wordPop, wordPopBackdrop, wpHistory = [], wpIndex = -1 (module-level singletons)
chapter-app.js:2010-2017 renderWordPop creates wordPop ONCE, then reuses it
chapter-app.js:2061 wordPop.innerHTML = '' — content is destroyed and rebuilt per render
chapter-app.js:2099 const headwordEl = el('div', { class: 'word-pop-de', style: 'color:' + color }) — a NEW element per render
chapter-app.js:2100 headwordEl.appendChild(germanWordSpans(t.w)) — the headword text is ALWAYS the clicked token’s own word
chapter-app.js:2414-2417 is-open is added inside requestAnimationFrame — NOT observable synchronously, so unusable by a synchronous detector
chapter-app.js:976/1037/1190/1352/2878/2999 — every clickable span binds openWordPop(e, t, siblingTokens); the token object is passed by closure and never written to the DOM
step2_ownershipMechanism.existingIdentityMarkers: NONE. No data-* attribute, no lexeme id, and no popup→span backreference is written to the DOM. The token object exists only in the click closure.

signalsEvaluated.verdict: REJECTED by brief; also would not have helped, see step5
REJECTED in P28 — container is reused
TESTED AND REJECTED — see step4/step5. The element is indeed recreated on every render, but a render does NOT happen on every click, so a surviving node does not prove foreign ownership.

step3_fullPass.fidelity: reproduced the current detector exactly on 4 of 6 chapters (b2-15 3/3, a1-7 3/3, c1-26 3/3, b1-22 1/1). Two chapters differ from the P26 baseline: a1-8 measured 3 vs 4, a1-39 measured 0 vs 1 — index drift of the kind already characterised in P22/P23, not a harness defect.

step4_elementIdentity.observed: the .word-pop-de node was REUSED (not replaced) on 135 of the clicks across the six chapters, including on genuine findings
step4_elementIdentity.mechanism: a click on a node whose surface matches the popup already on screen does not trigger a re-render, so headEl survives. Element identity therefore distinguishes "a render happened" from "no render happened" — NOT "this popup is mine" from "this popup is someone else’s".

step5_candidateRule.rule: opened := (.word-pop-de element was replaced by this click)

successCriteria.1_obgleichFalsePositivesDisappear: the 3 did disappear — but this is no longer desirable, see revision below
successCriteria.5_lemmaCaseRemains: NOT APPLICABLE — no case-insensitive lemma case exists in 4,237 observed nodes
successCriteria.7_ownershipProven: FAIL — element identity proves render, not ownership

step5_candidateRule.verdict: REJECTED — it destroys 4 genuine findings (c1-26 ×3, b1-22 ×1)

phase27Revision.claim: the three b2-15 Obgleich findings are NOT detector false positives
phase27Revision.p27Evidence: clicking each node in isolation never produced a popup whose headword read "Obgleich" (5.1s polling), so the comparison looked cross-word
phase27Revision.p29Evidence: in the FAITHFUL full pass the popup headword for all three is "obgleich" — the same lexeme, differing only in case (prevHead "obgleich", headText "obgleich", case-insensitive match true). The popup belongs to the clicked word.
phase27Revision.whyP27WasWrong: selective-index probing clicked .wp-close and waited between nodes, which left the popup in a state the engine never reaches. The isolation probe perturbed the very state it was measuring.
phase27Revision.correctedClassification: the 3 records are the SAME class as G2/G3 — an occurrence-role vs lexeme-class colour difference (span object green vs headword adjective amber for a concessive conjunction). They belong with DATA/AUTHORING, and the P26/P27 note that the exercise chips render r-object while the chapter authors r-konz remains the actual defect.
phase27Revision.confidence: PROVEN by the faithful full pass; supersedes audit/obgleich-live-p27.json on this point (that file is NOT modified)
phase27Revision.consequence: there is currently NO known HCM detector false positive, so no detector fix is warranted at all. The disposition returns to 16 BY-DESIGN + 21 DATA/AUTHORING = 37.

step7_noSafeSignal.conclusion: No reliable popup ownership signal was found in the existing architecture.
step7_noSafeSignal.smallestInstrumentationThatWouldExposeOw: in renderWordPop (chapter-app.js:2010), stamp the popup with the word it was rendered for and a monotonic render counter — e.g. wordPop.dataset.wpWord = t.w; wordPop.dataset.wpRender = String(++renderSeq). A detector then proves ownership by reading dataset.wpWord against the clicked surface and dataset.wpRender against the value captured before the click. Two lines, no behavioural change, no learner-visible effect.
step7_noSafeSignal.butAlsoNotNeeded: given the Phase-27 revision there is no false positive to fix, so this instrumentation is only worth adding if a genuine cross-word case is ever demonstrated.

recommendation: do NOT change qa-engine.js — no false positive is established
treat the 3 b2-15 records as DATA/AUTHORING alongside D1/D2 in audit/hcm-data-correction-plan-p28.json (that plan is unchanged and does not yet include them)
if a future phase wants ownership certainty, add the two-line dataset stamp above before touching the detector
